title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M is a rank-2 module over a base S, and G(M) is GL(M). The fixed sections rho and sigma of G(M) satisfy the genericity hypotheses of the previous page: 1, rho^{-1}, N_1 are linearly independent on each fibre, likewise 1, sigma^{-1}, N_1, and Tr(N_1 rho) is invertible, normalised to 1. There are two unipotent elements eps_0 = 1+N_0 and eps_1 = 1+N_1 with int(rho)eps_0 = int(sigma)eps_0 = eps_1. Equivalently rho N_0 rho^{-1} = sigma N_0 sigma^{-1} = N_1. One has N_1 rho = -N_1 sigma = rho+sigma.

Groups. B_0 is a 'Borel' normalising the additive line L_0 = eps_0(G_a), with exact sequence 1 -> L_0 -> B_0 -(det)-> G_m -> 1, and u in B_0 acts by u N_0 u^{-1} = det(u) N_0. B'_0 is the subgroup scheme cut out by (74).

This page. The morphism B'_0 -> G(M) x G(M) x G_m, u |-> ([u,rho], [u,sigma], det u), lands in X_{rho,sigma}. That is the scheme of solutions (xi, eta, mu) of the simultaneous equations (33)-(35); in view of (82bis) on the next page these are presumably xi = eta * eps_1(mu-1) together with conditions making xi, eta 'commutators with rho, sigma'. The map induces an isomorphism (79): B'_0 ≅ X_{rho,sigma}.

Corollary (recalled 'pour mémoire'):
- The projection (xi, eta, mu) |-> xi is a monomorphism. Its image is {xi : det xi = 1, Tr(xi rho) = Tr rho, Tr(xi(rho+sigma)) invertible}.
- Similarly for eta, with sigma in place of rho.
- (80): Tr xi(rho+sigma) = Tr eta(rho+sigma) = 1/mu.

Check of (80). Note rho+sigma = N_1 rho and rho^{-1} N_1 rho = N_0. Then Tr([u,rho] N_1 rho) = Tr(u rho u^{-1} N_0) = Tr(rho u^{-1} N_0 u) = det(u)^{-1} Tr(rho N_0) = det(u)^{-1} Tr(N_1 rho) = 1/det u. So mu = det u, consistent with the normalisation.

The margin identity -N_1 sigma = N_1 rho = rho N_0 = -sigma N_0 records exactly these relations.

Scholie. Transport of structure gives X_{rho,sigma} a group structure. The next page makes it explicit via the cocycle identity [u'u, rho] = u'[u,rho]u'^{-1} [u',rho].

Purpose. This is a step in solving the 'loop equation' (82): alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = beta sigma(beta)^{-1} eps_1(mu-1) in rank 2. The page reduces the problem to the fibration G_{rho,sigma} -> X_{rho,sigma} ≅ B'_0 and identifies the base with an explicit solvable group scheme.
errors: The corollary writes the source as X_rho; context (and the triple (xi,eta,mu)) indicates X_{rho,sigma} — a notational slip or abbreviation.

Minor: (33)-(35) are not visible here, so the exact form of the defining equations of X_{rho,sigma} is inferred; the claimed iso and image description are consistent with the computations checked (det, trace, and (80) all verify).

ideas.what: Commutators [u,rho] in GL_2 characterised by det=1 and Tr(xi rho)=Tr rho, with injectivity of u -> [u,rho] on a suitable Borel-type subgroup

ideas.what: Solution scheme X_{rho,sigma} of a rank-2 'loop equation' identified with a solvable subgroup scheme B'_0 (extension of G_m by G_a), with transported group law given by the cocycle rule xi''=u'(xi)xi'
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/stabiliser description of solution schemes of twisted commutator equations; Borel subgroup scheme
